title: Soft-boot orchestration for tenant-prioritized prewarming and KV cache warming
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: Dedicated fleets still see high p95 cold-start latencies for low-traffic tenants and bursty workloads because entire weight residency or KV priming is gated behind full allocation. Goal: Implement a soft-boot orchestration layer that allows nodes to reach a usable operating point faster by (1) controlled lightweight weight staging, (2) KV prefix priming at small granularity, and (3) tenant-priority admission so SLO-bound tenants get earlier soft-boot slots. Deliverables: orchestration controller, admission policy, API surface for Dedicated configs, metrics & dashboards, e2e tests and a gradual rollout plan across fleets.
acceptance_criteria: p95 cold-start generation latency for low-traffic tenants improves by >= 40% in a mixed-tenant cluster under synthetic burst tests
Throughput guarantees honored: tenants that opt into priority soft-boot must achieve configured RPS within 60s of burst start in 95% of trials
KV cache hit ratio for primed prefixes increases by >= 30% for primed tenants within 2 minutes of admission
No regression in high-capacity tenants' latency or throughput (>1% error budget increase across monitored fleets)
Integration tests covering weight staging failure modes (partial load, interrupted staging) and graceful fallback to cold boot
design_decisions: Use a staged weight load: metadata-first then lazy streaming of large weight shards. This reduces time-to-first-token while allowing full model quality to converge.
KV priming will operate at prefix granularity (configurable prefix length) and support progressive commitments (soft -> full prime).
Admission policy is tenant-credit-aware: tenants can reserve soft-boot slots via Dedicated config; unreserved capacity used opportunistically and preemptable by higher-priority tenants.
Controller runs as part of the Dedicated control plane with a reconciliation loop and backoff policies to avoid thundering herd on shared storage.
Fallback behavior: if soft-boot fails or stalls beyond threshold, controller triggers a full cold-start path and logs detailed triage info for postmortem.
We avoid cross-tenant weight diffusion: staged loading must still enforce tenant weight isolation to meet data residency and security requirements.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Canary in staging with deterministic synthetic workload (2 nodes, 3 tenants) — validate acceptance criteria locally (2 weeks)
Phase 1: Internal canary on non-production fleets (5% of Dedicated capacity) with observability on p50/p95/p99 latency and KV hit ratios (1 week)
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 25% with opt-in tenant list (customers with throughput SLAs) — run A/B test against control fleets (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Global rollout with automatic throttles and kill-switch in control plane (toggle via Console) (1 week)
Contingency: automatic rollback criteria include >1% overall error budget burn or persistent throughput degradation for enterprise tenants for >10 minutes
monitoring: New metrics: soft_boot_time_seconds, kv_prime_prefixes_count, kv_prime_hit_rate_by_tenant, soft_boot_failure_count
Dashboards: Dedicated > Warmup > Per-tenant soft-boot overview (p50/p95 latency, time-to-meet-RPS, KV hit curves)
Alerts: soft_boot_failure_count > 5 in 5m for a fleet; kv_prime_hit_rate_by_tenant < 10% after 3 minutes for an opted-in tenant
Tracing: add tags for stage (metadata, shard-stream, kv-prime) to existing request traces and warm orchestration spans
SLO verification: run nightly synthetic bursts to compute daily p95 cold-start regressions and compare to baseline
